items.challenge: Incumbent wealth can migrate into real assets, foreign assets, corporations or synthetic K exposure, neutralizing a simple wallet cap.
items.implication: Anti-concentration analysis must use ultimate beneficial economic exposure and cannot rely on wallet balances alone.

items.challenge: Expertise-weighted voting can be captured through credential gaming, Goodhart effects, coordinated blocs or biased integrity scoring.
items.implication: Require bounded weights, transparent scoring, conflict disclosure, appeal, adversarial audit and plural evidence.

items.challenge: UBI indexation can become pro-inflationary when real supply is constrained.
items.implication: Tie protection to real capacity, targeted services and automatic stabilizer logic rather than a mechanically escalating nominal payment.

items.challenge: A dominant K_M could recreate banking leverage, maturity transformation and systemic risk even if the base asset is not debt.
items.implication: Credit-market and lender-of-last-resort/liquidity architecture require separate prudential design.

items.challenge: Currency substitution can generate capital flight, balance-sheet mismatches and political/legal resistance.
items.implication: Transition paths must model jurisdiction, contract denomination and sectoral balance sheets rather than only aggregate exchange rates.

items.challenge: Central online settlement creates operational concentration and privacy/surveillance risks.
items.implication: Operational replication, least-privilege data design, auditability, privacy architecture and failure recovery are required.

items.challenge: A globally dominant unit requires a deep safe-asset and collateral ecosystem, not only high token demand.
items.implication: State S5 and beyond require explicit credit, collateral, term structure and liquidity institutions.
